messages.author: e3daea24651c4835
messages.subject: decrease verbosity
parts:
Hi Henrik,

What is the correct way to decrease verbosity of the aroma.affymetrix
scripts? I've been trying to use verbose<-Arguments$getVerbose(xxx)
with different values, but it seems only to _increase_ verbosity :)

Thanks a lot!
Nicolas

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] decrease verbosity
parts:
On Tue, May 20, 2008 at 3:03 PM, Nicolas Stransky
<nicolas....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Henrik,
>
> What is the correct way to decrease verbosity of the aroma.affymetrix
> scripts? I've been trying to use verbose<-Arguments$getVerbose(xxx)
> with different values, but it seems only to _increase_ verbosity :)

The smaller number (-20 is smaller than -10), the more details. So,
verbose=0 (or FALSE) gives no details, verbose=-1 (TRUE) somewhat
more, verbose=-2 even more and so on. Think of the value as the
"threshold" that one has to overcome in order for output to be
displayed. [I guess the convention might be the other way around, but
unfortunately that's how it works now].

/Henrik

>
> Thanks a lot!
> Nicolas
>
> >
>

Nope, currently that's it.

You can also send all verbose output to file, by create a Verbose
object that writes to file (the default is to write to the standard
output connection), e.g.

verbose <- Verbose(con="myAnalysis.log", threshold=-10, timestamp=TRUE);

[It's on my wish list to have a parallel ProgressBar reporting the
progress in a more compact way and have the verbose output go to a
file or similar.]

Cheers

/Henrik

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: decrease verbosity
parts:
Hi,

ok, I finally tracked this down. There is a statement in fit() for
ProbeLevelModel (the same for FirmaModel), that looks like this:

if (verbose) {
print(this);
...
}

This does not write to the Verbose object and assumes that you only
write to stdout. I've replaced the above to be print(verbose, this).

This will fix be in the next release.

Cheers

Henrik
